claims.title: Phoenician colonisation of the coast
claims.summary: Phoenician traders founded Gadir (modern Cádiz) and other settlements, drawing Iberia into Mediterranean commerce and bringing eastern goods, writing and urban contact to the peninsula.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1100bce-phoenician-colonisation-of-the-coast, claim TL:ESP:event:1100bce:phoenician-colonisation-of-the-coast, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rome enters Hispania
claims.summary: During the Second Punic War, Roman forces landed in Iberia; over roughly two centuries Rome conquered the entire peninsula and organised it as the provinces of Hispania.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-218bce-rome-enters-hispania, claim TL:ESP:event:218bce:rome-enters-hispania, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Germanic peoples enter Iberia
claims.summary: As Roman power waned, Germanic groups crossed into the peninsula; the Visigoths emerged as the dominant power and built a kingdom on the Roman and Christian inheritance.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-409-germanic-peoples-enter-iberia, claim TL:ESP:event:409:germanic-peoples-enter-iberia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Visigothic kingdom of Toledo turns Catholic
claims.summary: At the Third Council of Toledo, King Reccared and the Visigoths converted from Arian to Catholic Christianity, binding the ruling Germanic elite to the Hispano-Roman Catholic population.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-589-visigothic-kingdom-of-toledo-turns-catholic, claim TL:ESP:event:589:visigothic-kingdom-of-toledo-turns-catholic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Umayyad conquest and the Battle of Guadalete
claims.summary: An Umayyad army under Tariq ibn Ziyad defeated and killed the Visigothic king Roderic, opening the way to the rapid Muslim conquest of most of the peninsula and the creation of Al-Andalus.

sources.label: The Art of the Umayyad Period in Spain (711–1031)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-711-umayyad-conquest-and-the-battle-of-guadalete, claim TL:ESP:event:711:umayyad-conquest-and-the-battle-of-guadalete, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Caliphate of Córdoba proclaimed
claims.summary: Abd al-Rahman III declared himself caliph at Córdoba, marking the political and cultural zenith of Al-Andalus, whose capital became a leading centre of learning and the arts in Europe.

sources.label: The Art of the Umayyad Period in Spain (711–1031)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-929-caliphate-of-cordoba-proclaimed, claim TL:ESP:event:929:caliphate-of-cordoba-proclaimed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Christian capture of Toledo
claims.summary: Alfonso VI of León and Castile took the former Visigothic capital of Toledo, a major advance of the Reconquista and a centre where Arabic, Hebrew and Latin learning was later translated.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1085-christian-capture-of-toledo, claim TL:ESP:event:1085:christian-capture-of-toledo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
claims.summary: A coalition of Christian kingdoms decisively defeated the Almohad caliphate, breaking Muslim power in the peninsula and accelerating the southward Christian advance.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1212-battle-of-las-navas-de-tolosa, claim TL:ESP:event:1212:battle-of-las-navas-de-tolosa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of Granada
claims.summary: Muhammad XII (Boabdil) surrendered Granada, the last Muslim state in Iberia, to the Catholic Monarchs, completing the Reconquista after nearly eight centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1492-fall-of-granada, claim TL:ESP:event:1492:fall-of-granada, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Marriage of Isabella and Ferdinand
claims.summary: The union of Isabella of Castile and Ferdinand of Aragon joined the two leading Iberian crowns, creating the dynastic foundation of a unified Spain under the 'Catholic Monarchs'.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1469-marriage-of-isabella-and-ferdinand, claim TL:ESP:event:1469:marriage-of-isabella-and-ferdinand, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Establishment of the Spanish Inquisition
claims.summary: Authorised under the Catholic Monarchs, the Spanish Inquisition prosecuted suspected heretics, especially conversos, through trials, torture and executions, enforcing religious uniformity for centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1478-establishment-of-the-spanish-inquisition, claim TL:ESP:event:1478:establishment-of-the-spanish-inquisition, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Columbus's first voyage and the Alhambra Decree
claims.summary: Columbus reached the Americas under the crown of Castile, beginning Spain's overseas empire; the same year the Alhambra Decree expelled Spain's Jews who refused conversion.

sources.label: Aniversario de los decretos de expulsión de los judíos de los reinos de Castilla y Aragón
sources.publisher: Portal de Archivos de Andalucía, Junta de Andalucía

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1492-columbus-s-first-voyage-and-the-alhambra-decree, claim TL:ESP:event:1492:columbus-s-first-voyage-and-the-alhambra-decree, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Conquest of the Aztec Empire
claims.summary: Hernán Cortés and allied forces overthrew the Aztec empire, a conquest that brought vast wealth to Spain alongside war, subjugation and a catastrophic collapse of Indigenous populations.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1519-conquest-of-the-aztec-empire, claim TL:ESP:event:1519:conquest-of-the-aztec-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reign of Philip II
claims.summary: Philip II ruled Spain at the height of its imperial power, made Madrid the capital and defended Catholicism in Europe's wars, presiding over the cultural Golden Age despite the defeat of the Armada in 1588.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1556-reign-of-philip-ii, claim TL:ESP:event:1556:reign-of-philip-ii, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of Charles II and end of the Spanish Habsburgs
claims.summary: The childless death of Charles II ended Habsburg rule in Spain. His will bequeathed the throne to the Bourbon Philip of Anjou, triggering a European war of succession.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1700-death-of-charles-ii-and-end-of-the-spanish, claim TL:ESP:event:1700:death-of-charles-ii-and-end-of-the-spanish, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: War of the Spanish Succession
claims.summary: A European war over the Spanish throne ended with the Bourbon Philip V confirmed as king by the Treaty of Utrecht (1713), which stripped Spain of its European territories and Gibraltar.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1701-war-of-the-spanish-succession, claim TL:ESP:event:1701:war-of-the-spanish-succession, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Dos de Mayo uprising
claims.summary: The people of Madrid rose against the occupying French army; the brutal repression that followed ignited the Peninsular War, Spain's war of independence against Napoleon.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1808-dos-de-mayo-uprising, claim TL:ESP:event:1808:dos-de-mayo-uprising, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Constitution of Cádiz
claims.summary: Liberal deputies meeting in besieged Cádiz promulgated Spain's first constitution, asserting national sovereignty and a separation of powers, though it was abolished by Ferdinand VII in 1814.

sources.label: Constitution of the Spanish Monarchy, enacted in Cádiz, 19 March 1812

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1812-constitution-of-cadiz, claim TL:ESP:event:1812:constitution-of-cadiz, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: End of the Peninsular War
claims.summary: Allied Spanish, British and Portuguese forces expelled the French and restored Spanish independence, but the returning Ferdinand VII reimposed absolute monarchy and revoked the 1812 constitution.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1814-end-of-the-peninsular-war, claim TL:ESP:event:1814:end-of-the-peninsular-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Loss of the American mainland empire
claims.summary: Independence movements across Spanish America broke away during and after the Napoleonic crisis, ending Spain's three-century rule over most of the Americas.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1810-loss-of-the-american-mainland-empire, claim TL:ESP:event:1810:loss-of-the-american-mainland-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Disaster of 1898
claims.summary: Defeat in the Spanish-American War ended Spain's overseas empire; under the Treaty of Paris it lost Cuba, Puerto Rico, the Philippines and Guam, a trauma that shaped a generation.

sources.label: The World of 1898: The Spanish-American War

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1898-the-disaster-of-1898, claim TL:ESP:event:1898:the-disaster-of-1898, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Proclamation of the Second Republic
claims.summary: After King Alfonso XIII left Spain, republicans proclaimed the Second Spanish Republic, which pursued reform amid intense political and social polarisation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1931-proclamation-of-the-second-republic, claim TL:ESP:event:1931:proclamation-of-the-second-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Spanish Civil War
claims.summary: A military coup against the Republic led by Franco failed to seize power outright and triggered a devastating civil war, fuelled by foreign intervention and marked by mass atrocities; the Nationalists won in 1939.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1936-spanish-civil-war, claim TL:ESP:event:1936:spanish-civil-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Franco dictatorship
claims.summary: Franco ruled Spain as an authoritarian dictator for nearly four decades, repressing opponents and regional identities, before later decades brought economic growth and cautious opening to the West.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1939-the-franco-dictatorship, claim TL:ESP:event:1939:the-franco-dictatorship, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of Franco and accession of Juan Carlos I
claims.summary: Franco's death brought King Juan Carlos I to the throne; rather than continue the dictatorship, the king became a key figure in steering Spain toward democracy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1975-death-of-franco-and-accession-of-juan-carlos-i, claim TL:ESP:event:1975:death-of-franco-and-accession-of-juan-carlos-i, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First free elections since the Civil War
claims.summary: Spain held its first democratic elections in over four decades, producing a parliament that would draft a new constitution under Prime Minister Adolfo Suárez.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1977-first-free-elections-since-the-civil-war, claim TL:ESP:event:1977:first-free-elections-since-the-civil-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Spanish Constitution of 1978
claims.summary: Ratified by referendum on 6 December and promulgated on 29 December 1978, the constitution established a parliamentary monarchy, fundamental rights and a state of autonomous communities.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1978-spanish-constitution-of-1978, claim TL:ESP:event:1978:spanish-constitution-of-1978, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Accession to the European Communities
claims.summary: Spain joined the European Communities (now the European Union), anchoring its democracy in European integration and ushering in decades of modernisation and growth.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Spain: From the crossroads of Iberia to a modern European democracy.", terralore.co/country/ESP/chronicle#ev-1986-accession-to-the-european-communities, claim TL:ESP:event:1986:accession-to-the-european-communities, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
